detail.body:
## Motivation

Two independent, unrelated-but-small fixes found:

1. Partial rotary embeddings crash on XPU's fallback kernel path.
2. Custom remote-code tokenizers with a stale `_pad()` override crashing on every request once `padding_side` started being forwarded (found via `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`).

## Modifications

### 1. `RotaryEmbedding.forward_xpu()` partial rotary embeddings (`python/sglang/srt/layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`)

The fallback-kernel branch (used when `head_size` is not in `[128, 256, 512]`) calls `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding(...)` without slicing to `rotary_dim` first. That compiled kernel asserts `rotary_dim == head_size` internally and raises `RuntimeError: Rotary dim doesn't match query head_size` for any model with partial rotary embeddings (`rotary_dim < head_size`) on XPU, e.g. `adept/persimmon-8b-chat`, `microsoft/phi-2`, `stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b`, `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t`, `stabilityai/stablelm-zephyr-3b`. Independent of `--attention-backend`, since rotary embedding dispatch is keyed on device type (`is_xpu()`).

Fix: add an `elif self.head_size != self.rotary_dim` branch that falls back to `forward_native()`, mirroring the existing pattern where `forward_cpu`/`forward_npu` already fall back to `forward_native` for their own unsupported cases.

### 2. Tokenizer `_pad()` compat shim for stale custom signatures (`python/sglang/srt/utils/patch_tokenizer.py`)

transformers 5.x's `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.pad()` now always forwards `padding_side` down to `_pad()`. Custom remote-code tokenizers with a stale, fixed `_pad()` signature (no `padding_side` param, no `**kwargs` catch-all -- e.g. `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`'s `ChatGLMTokenizer`, unchanged for years) crash with:

```
TypeError: ChatGLMTokenizer._pad() got an unexpected keyword argument 'padding_side'
```

on every single generation request, regardless of memory/backend settings.

Fix: detects the mismatch structurally via `inspect.signature` (not a name/class check), so any other custom tokenizer with the same stale signature is covered too, and wraps `_pad()` to drop the `padding_side` kwarg before delegating to the original implementation (which already reads `self.padding_side` directly, so behavior is unchanged). Also adds `_PadPaddingSideShim.unpatch()`, wired into the shared `unpatch_tokenizer()` entrypoint, so the pad shim no longer leaks across test/tokenizer instances.

## Accuracy Tests

Both fixes were validated end-to-end on real Intel XPU hardware, not just reasoned about statically:

- **Rotary fix**: 20-example accuracy smoke checks (server + client, real GPU) for `adept/persimmon-8b-chat` (intel_xpu backend, gsm8k), `microsoft/phi-2` (triton backend, gsm8k), `stabilityai/stablelm-3b-4e1t` (triton backend, hellaswag), `stabilityai/stablelm-zephyr-3b` (triton backend, gsm8k) -- all previously crashed with `RuntimeError: Rotary dim doesn't match query head_size`, all now serve and produce results.
- **Tokenizer `_pad()` shim**: confirmed on real Intel XPU hardware against `zai-org/chatglm2-6b`: the `TypeError` no longer occurs and generation requests proceed past tokenization/padding to a correct completion.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Both fixes are either startup-time compatibility shims or exception-path corrections -- neither touches inference-loop math or kernels.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit) guide -- `pre-commit run` passes clean on every changed file.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests) guide -- added for the tokenizer `_pad()` shim (patch/unpatch lifecycle, idempotency, per-call override, restoration on raise); the rotary fix was validated by reproducing the original crash on real hardware and confirming it's gone (see Accuracy Tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) -- not applicable; both are internal bug fixes with no user-facing API or CLI changes.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) -- see Accuracy Tests above; no speed impact.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Closes #41088. Supersedes and replaces #41796 (folded in here at the author's request to land together; that PR will be closed in favor of this PR).

The `UnifiedRadixCache.dec_lock_ref` fix originally bundled here has been dropped from this PR per review feedback (the "restore the default" approach could mask a real missing-receipt bug); that fix is tracked separately in #41142.

+def _needs_pad_padding_side_shim(tokenizer) -> bool:

@@ -40,6 +62,49 @@ def decode_without_hf_kwargs(tokenizer, token_ids, skip_special_tokens):
     return tokenizer.decode(token_ids)
 
 
+class _PadPaddingSideShim:
+    _PATCHED_FLAG = "_sglang_pad_padding_side_patched"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def patch(cls, tokenizer):
+        tokenizer_cls = type(tokenizer)
+
+        if getattr(tokenizer_cls, cls._PATCHED_FLAG, False):
+            return tokenizer
+
+        original_pad = tokenizer_cls._pad
+
+        def patched_pad(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            padding_side = kwargs.pop("padding_side", None)
+            if padding_side is None or padding_side == self.padding_side:
+                return original_pad(self, *args, **kwargs)
+            previous_padding_side = self.padding_side
+            self.padding_side = padding_side
+            try:
+                return original_pad(self, *args, **kwargs)
+            finally:
+                self.padding_side = previous_padding_side
+
+        tokenizer_cls._original_pad = original_pad
+        tokenizer_cls._pad = patched_pad
+        setattr(tokenizer_cls, cls._PATCHED_FLAG, True)
+
+        return tokenizer
+
+    @classmethod
+    def unpatch(cls, tokenizer):
+        tokenizer_cls = type(tokenizer)
+
+        if not getattr(tokenizer_cls, cls._PATCHED_FLAG, False):
+            return tokenizer
+
+        tokenizer_cls._pad = tokenizer_cls._original_pad
+        del tokenizer_cls._original_pad
+        delattr(tokenizer_cls, cls._PATCHED_FLAG)
+
+        return tokenizer
+
+
 class _SpecialTokensCachePatcher:
     _PATCHED_FLAG = "_sglang_special_tokens_patched"
     _CACHED_TOKENS_ATTR = "_sglang_cached_special_tokens"

+class TestPadPaddingSideShimUnitTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_patch_unpatch_restores_original(self):
+        tokenizer = _FakeStaleTokenizer()
+        cls = type(tokenizer)
+        original_pad = cls._pad
+
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+        self.addCleanup(unpatch_tokenizer, tokenizer)
+        self.assertTrue(getattr(cls, "_sglang_pad_padding_side_patched", False))
+        self.assertIsNot(cls._pad, original_pad)
+
+        unpatch_tokenizer(tokenizer)
+        self.assertFalse(getattr(cls, "_sglang_pad_padding_side_patched", False))
+        self.assertIs(cls._pad, original_pad)
+
+    def test_double_patch_is_idempotent(self):
+        tokenizer = _FakeStaleTokenizer()
+        cls = type(tokenizer)
+
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+        self.addCleanup(unpatch_tokenizer, tokenizer)
+        patched_once = cls._pad
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+
+        self.assertIs(cls._pad, patched_once)
+        self.assertTrue(getattr(cls, "_sglang_pad_padding_side_patched", False))
+
+    def test_patch_applies_to_all_instances_of_the_class(self):
+        tokenizer_a = _FakeStaleTokenizer(padding_side="left")
+        tokenizer_b = _FakeStaleTokenizer(padding_side="right")
+        self.assertIs(type(tokenizer_a), type(tokenizer_b))
+
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer_a)
+        try:
+            self.assertTrue(
+                getattr(type(tokenizer_b), "_sglang_pad_padding_side_patched", False)
+            )
+
+            tokenizer_a._pad({"input_ids": [1]})
+            tokenizer_b._pad({"input_ids": [2]})
+
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer_a.pad_calls[-1][1], "left")
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer_b.pad_calls[-1][1], "right")
+        finally:
+            unpatch_tokenizer(tokenizer_a)
+
+    def test_per_call_padding_side_override_applied_and_restored(self):
+        tokenizer = _FakeStaleTokenizer(padding_side="right")
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+        try:
+            tokenizer._pad({"input_ids": [1]}, padding_side="left")
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer.pad_calls[-1][1], "left")
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer.padding_side, "right")
+        finally:
+            unpatch_tokenizer(tokenizer)
+
+    def test_padding_side_override_matching_default_is_noop(self):
+        tokenizer = _FakeStaleTokenizer(padding_side="right")
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+        try:
+            tokenizer._pad({"input_ids": [1]}, padding_side="right")
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer.pad_calls[-1][1], "right")
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer.padding_side, "right")
+        finally:
+            unpatch_tokenizer(tokenizer)
+
+    def test_none_padding_side_passes_through(self):
+        tokenizer = _FakeStaleTokenizer(padding_side="right")
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+        try:
+            tokenizer._pad({"input_ids": [1]})
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer.pad_calls[-1][1], "right")
+        finally:
+            unpatch_tokenizer(tokenizer)
+
+    def test_padding_side_restored_after_pad_raises(self):
+        tokenizer = _FakeRaisingTokenizer(padding_side="right")
+        _PadPaddingSideShim.patch(tokenizer)
+        try:
+            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+                tokenizer._pad(padding_side="left")
+            self.assertEqual(tokenizer.padding_side, "right")
+        finally:
+            unpatch_tokenizer(tokenizer)
+
+
+class _FakeStaleTokenizer:
